subject: Pricing & batching follow-up — Redwood demo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing & batching follow-up — Redwood demo

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size pricing properly:

1) Recap of what we saw: continuous batching use case for customer support reranking + first-line triage. You mentioned a steady stream of user queries (not big spikes) and long-ish responses for context (average model response ~220 tokens).

2) Key qual questions we discussed (please confirm):
   - Monthly token volume: ~40M–60M tokens (prompt + response) across production traffic
   - Peak concurrency: typically small (5–10 concurrent requests), but you expect sustained throughput across minutes rather than second-scale spikes
   - Average prompt size: ~80 tokens, average response: ~220 tokens -> ~300 tokens per request on average
   - SLA/budget: target unit economics in the range of $600–$1,000 per 1M tokens (you said the team wants to get to a target $/1M tokens that keeps cost+infra within your per-seat budget)

3) Continuous batching assumptions we want to validate:
   - Workload pattern: relatively even arrival rate across core hours (08:00–20:00 PT) with modest diurnal variation; not many large bursts
   - Continuous batching expected to save ~20–40% of token compute cost compared to naive per-request serving for this profile (depending on cache hit rate and batch window)
   - Concurrency is low enough that batching windows of 50–200ms are feasible without adding noticeable latency

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the monthly token band (40M–60M) and whether that includes pre/post-processing tokens?
- Share any non-chat flow volumes (async bulk reranks, nightly batch jobs) if present — those can change cost expectations a lot.
- I attached our latest pricing deck and a SOC2 evidence checklist (for procurement). I’ll loop in Camila and Aditya from solutions/AM to help with the technical sizing and to propose a target $/1M tokens and a tailored Dedicated suggestion if needed.

Thanks — Marissa

--

Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up — Redwood demo

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few confirmations and clarifications:

- Monthly tokens: around 50M total (that includes prompt + response for the realtime support flow).
- We do have a nightly bulk rerank job that touches roughly 10M tokens/month (offline), separate from realtime.
- Concurrency: production realtime qps peaks at ~12 requests/sec very briefly during flash sales, but sustained concurrency is 6–8. Most requests are short waits (we need sub-500ms p95).
- Target budget: interested in a target of ~$750 per 1M tokens (we can flex depending on SLA and dedication options). That target would make the ROI work for us.

Happy to have Aditya look at sample traces/latency budgets. I’ll also get procurement to review the SOC2 checklist — thanks for including it.

— Alex

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up — Redwood demo

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround and the numbers. Summarizing qualification for the proposed sizing work: 

- Confirmed monthly tokens (prod realtime): 50M tokens
- Offline batch rerank: 10M tokens/month (can be handled as scheduled jobs)
- Working average tokens/request: ~300 tokens/request -> implies ~166k realtime requests/month (50M / 300)
- Budget target: ~$750 per 1M tokens (we'll size options around Hosted vs Dedicated to hit that unit-cost goal)
- Concurrency/latency: sustained concurrency ~6–8; short bursts to ~12; p95 latency requirement <500ms for user-facing flows

How we intend to model savings from continuous batching and other levers:
- Continuous batching: for an even-ish arrival rate and 6–8 sustained concurrency, we typically see 15–30% reduction in per-token compute cost after accounting for batching windows and KV cache effectiveness. We'll run a small simulation with your exact token distribution (Aditya will do this).
- Caching: if you have repeated prefixes or template prompts for support, KV/prefix cache can reduce prompt token compute by a measurable % — please share sample prompt templates if possible.
- Quantization/variant models: if we can tolerate a minor quality delta, switching to a quantized variant for reranking can reduce serving cost further.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Aditya — can you run a quick sim using the following inputs: 50M realtime tokens, 10M offline tokens, average 300 tokens/request, sustained concurrency 8, burst concurrency 12, target p95 <500ms. Please include batching window assumptions of 50ms, 100ms, and 200ms and show cost delta for each.
2) Marissa — I'll draft a Hosted vs Dedicated cost estimate around the $750/1M target and include the impact of continuous batching + caching.
3) Alex/Priya — can you share a sample of typical prompt templates (sanitized) and any latency traces so Aditya can parameterize the sim?

I attached the SOC2 checklist for procurement and the pricing deck Marissa referenced.

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeretail.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmeretail.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up — Redwood demo

Thanks all — I ran a quick back-of-envelope sim and will follow up with a spreadsheet by EOD. Initial findings (very rough):

- Baseline: 60M total tokens (50M realtime + 10M offline) at naive per-request serving -> baseline compute units X (we'll convert to $/1M later)
- Continuous batching (50ms window): ~12% reduction in compute cost vs baseline
- Continuous batching (100ms window): ~20% reduction
- Continuous batching (200ms window): ~25–30% reduction (latency impact small for offline and acceptable for realtime if we stay below 200ms in most cases)
- With KV/prefix cache (assume 15% prompt token saving) + batching (100ms) we can realistically hit ~30–40% overall compute saving vs naive baseline — moves effective unit cost close to your $750/1M target depending on model choice and quantization

I'll upload the spreadsheet (simulation inputs + cost model) to the Drive link and share the Drive file name shortly. If Alex/Priya can share sanitized prompt templates and a few p95 latency traces, I can parameterize the sim to be more precise.

-Aditya

Attachments: SOC2-audit-request.xlsx
